purpose: Qualify the exact condition under which query-head attention salience may be reduced onto shared physical GQA cache heads before applying the clean-room adaptive budget allocator.

sources.use: the paper defines a shared-norm retained-attention-mass bound and specifies arithmetic-mean salience within a GQA group
the pinned code accepts mean or max group reduction and applies a separately ambiguous safeguard
qualified physical-head allocator and exhaustive oracle

source_disposition.paper_statement: Section 3.5 uses the arithmetic mean of query-head attention weights within each GQA group as the physical-cache-head selection criterion.
source_disposition.code_statement: The pinned implementation defaults its CLI to mean but also accepts max; this protocol does not treat those choices as equivalent.
source_disposition.speck_derivation: For equal-size groups and the paper's single shared maximum transformed-value norm C, mean is sum divided by one common positive constant and therefore preserves the physical slot ordering that minimizes the query-head bound.

input_contract.query_salience: rectangular K-by-G-by-T finite non-negative weights: K physical KV heads, exactly G query heads sharing each physical head, and T candidate token slots
input_contract.normalization: reduction and allocation accept unnormalized salience; every query-head row must sum to one when evaluating the query-level eviction bound
input_contract.equal_group_size: G is identical for every physical head; unequal groups are outside the mean/sum equivalence claim
input_contract.group_identity: physical head k owns query heads k*G through (k+1)*G-1; ordering is representational and cannot change reductions
input_contract.budget: integer B in [0,K*T] counts physical KV token slots, never replicated query-head slots
input_contract.scope: one layer and one already-observed salience tensor; observation windows, pooling, recency retention, cross-layer allocation, and question-aware versus question-agnostic acquisition are excluded

derivation.shared_indicator: I[k,t] is one physical eviction decision and therefore applies to every query head q in group k
derivation.rank_equivalence: R_query=G*sum(k,t) I[k,t]*M[k,t]; because G is common, global top-B mean and sum select identical physical slots under identical tie-breaking
derivation.query_level_bound: for normalized query heads and one shared C, epsilon_query=2*K*G*C-2*C*R_query
limits: head-specific transformed-value/output norm weights require a weighted successor objective
unequal G requires summed or group-size-weighted salience rather than unweighted means
a smaller theoretical upper bound does not guarantee smaller realized output error or task loss

reference_contract.mean: arithmetic mean over the G query heads for each physical (head,token) slot
reference_contract.sum_control: arithmetic sum over the same group; must induce exactly the same budgets and selected identities as mean
reference_contract.max_negative_control: maximum over query heads; must be deterministic but receives no optimality authority and must lose to mean/sum on the frozen counterexample
reference_contract.allocation: pass reduced K-by-T salience to the qualified adaptive_head_budgets reference
reference_contract.query_mass: evaluate retained mass directly from the original K-by-G-by-T tensor and physical head budgets
reference_contract.bound: evaluate the query-level bound directly and verify equality with G times the physical-mean bound
reference_contract.tie_breaking: descending reduced weight, then ascending physical head, then ascending token

max_counterexample.purpose: disprove interchangeability of mean and max even with equal-size normalized groups

safeguard_disposition.paper: Algorithm 2 writes alpha*adaptive+(1-alpha)*uniform and reports alpha=0.2.
safeguard_disposition.pinned_code: The audited path computes round((1-floor_ratio)*adaptive+int(base_capacity*floor_ratio)) independently per head and checks conservation only before that operation.
safeguard_disposition.conservation_witness: For three heads, average capacity two, adaptive budgets (4,1,1), and floor_ratio 0.2, code-like rounding yields (3,1,1), total five rather than six.
safeguard_disposition.decision: exclude all safeguard mixing and integerization from this reference; require a separately frozen conservation-preserving successor

qualification_cases.weights: integer values zero through seven with deterministic ties; replace an all-zero query row at token zero before normalizing
qualification_cases.budgets: every integer from zero through K*T
qualification_cases.oracle: enumerate every feasible physical K-vector in [0,T]^K with sum B and maximize original query-head retained mass

success_gates: mean and sum reductions induce identical selected physical identities and head budgets in every random and special case
mean-based allocation attains the exhaustive maximum original query-head retained mass within 1e-12
direct query-level bound equals the scaled physical-mean bound within 1e-12 and never increases with budget
physical capacity is conserved for every allocation
max aggregation is deterministic and the frozen counterexample demonstrates strictly lower query-head retained mass
the safeguard witness demonstrates that independent code-like rounding is not conservation-safe
required_outputs: maximum mean-versus-sum reduction and retained-mass gaps
max counterexample selections and retained masses
safeguard witness budgets and conservation deficit

decision.failure: retain the result and block GQA use of the adaptive allocation baseline
decision.success: qualify only equal-size mean-reduced GQA as a clean-room reference primitive
